description: This is a monthly orientation held for people who are interested in enrolling in Survivorship Wellness, an 8-week clinical program focused on helping survivors of cancer learn about, set goals, and practice skills to optimize their health and wellness after cancer treatment. In this group program, you will have the opportunity to learn from and practice with our cancer center dieticians, social workers, psychologists, chaplains, health coaches, and exercise counselors to set goals around nutrition, physical activity, managing stress, sleeping well, and promoting sexual, emotional, and spiritual wellness after cancer treatment. This group is open to post-treatment UCSF cancer patients. Registration is required. Please call 415-353-3931 to learn more and to register. This program is covered by most insurance plans.

description: Indoor Air Quality – Mold in the Home Presented by: Timur Durani, MD Occupational and Environmental Medicine Specialist UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital Oakland Planners expect learners to: 1. Differentiate evidence-based health effects associated with indoor mold exposure from unvalidated claims regarding “toxic mold” and mycotoxin-related illness. 2. Evaluate patients with suspected mold exposure using an appropriate clinical approach, including recognition of allergies, hypersensitivity, and rare infectious manifestations. 3. Identify environmental, socioeconomic, housing-quality, and cultural factors that influence mold exposure risk and apply strategies to reduce implicit bias when evaluating patients with environmental health concerns. UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital Oakland is accredited by the California Medical Association to provide continuing medical education for physicians. UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital Oakland designates this live activity for a maximum of 1 AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™. Physicians should claim only the credit commensurate with the extent of their participation in the activity. ABP MOC Part 2 Points Successful completion of this CME activity, which includes participation in the evaluation component, enables the learner to earn up to 1 MOC point in the American Board of Pediatrics’ (ABP) Maintenance of Certification (MOC) program. It is the CME activity provider’s responsibility to submit learner completion information to ACCME for the purpose of granting ABP MOC credit. Contact Cristina.Fernandez@ucsf.edu for further details. ABS Continuous Certification (CC) Successful completion of this CME activity, which includes participation in the evaluation component, enables the learner to earn 1 credit toward the CME and Self-Assessment requirement(s) of the American Board of Surgery's Continuous Certification program. It is the CME activity provider's responsibility to submit learner completion information to ACCME for the purpose of granting ABS credit. Contact Cristina.Fernandez@ucsf.edu for further details. Zoom Participants: Please contact Cristina.Fernandez@ucsf.edu for webinar information. For CME credit, evaluations must be completed by 12pm on the Friday after Grand Rounds. Requests for the link to the current evaluation must be sent to Cristina.Fernandez@ucsf.edu by NOON on the day of Grand Rounds. description: What’s next in genomics workflows? Join us for a Lunch & Learn exploring the technologies and strategies that enable high-quality next-generation sequencing (NGS) data generation, improved reproducibility, and greater efficiency in genomics research. The session will highlight genomics workflows from sample preparation through NGS, including automation with Bravo systems, quality control using Fragment Analyzer and TapeStation systems, and SureSelect target enrichment solutions. Attendees will learn how these technologies work together to streamline workflows, improve data quality, and support a wide range of applications from basic research to translational genomics studies. The Agilent team will share insights into the latest tools and approaches for optimizing genomics workflows and enabling more reproducible sequencing results. The session will conclude with an open discussion about your research goals, current workflows, and the challenges you are facing in generating reliable sequencing data. Enjoy a complimentary lunch while connecting with colleagues and learning about the latest advances in genomics technologies. Seats are limited. Reserve your spot today: https://humangenetics.ucsf.edu/lunch-and-learn-tech-seminar-series-agilent We encourage you to share this invitation with colleagues and collaborators who may be interested. We look forward to seeing you!

description: SAVE THE DATE Neurodiagnostics Symposium Advancing Biomarker Discovery and Application September 23, 2026 | 9am-5pm Nancy Friend Pritzker Psychiatry Building Auditorium, UCSF Mission Bay We invite you to save the date for an all-day Neurodiagnostics Symposium which aims to convene the community working on molecular biomarkers across the neurosciences, make connections, and spur collaborations. We also hope to help folks who work on early biomarker discovery understand the process of advancing their candidate biomarkers to clinical use. The event will be divided into four sessions pertaining to the stages of diagnostic development: biomarker discovery, validation, clinical implementation, and scalability (including academic-industry partnerships). The event will conclude with a networking reception for continued conversation with colleagues.
